The sellers from the red day are trapped. It is short-term positioning and rarely an earnings day: an earnings-day gap is an earnings gapper, a baby red candle before a gap is just a breakout, and a gap against a downtrend is a different setup (owner rulings 2026-10-23/24).

lesson_text: High Volume Edge: an up day on a volume that DWARFS everything before it, ten times normal and above the prior record, often on a lesser-known name, the start of a new story; an earnings day counts when the volume is truly massive. That day's close is a LEVEL to mark on the chart, the price the biggest participants committed at; price may trade under it later. It is not an HVC (any high-volume close) and not a PEG (an earnings gap on big but ordinary volume); OPEX and month-end sessions do not count (owner rulings 2026-10-23/25). Here the stock closed up 18.23% on the heaviest volume of the lookback.

lesson_text: Oops Reversal (scanner version): opens below the prior close, trades under the prior day's low, then reverses and closes above the prior close. A Williams Oops opens below the prior LOW and rallies back above it. A Super Oops closes above the prior day's HIGH, engulfing the whole day. LOCATION is the main thing: it comes at the end of an orderly drift lower, a flag, a wedge, a double bottom or the end of a downtrend, into a buyable spot, with orderly days before it (no news gap, no outsized red bar) and a technical, not news-sized, Oops day; the Oops-day low must never break afterwards (owner rulings 2026-10-23/24). Here it opened 0.48% from the prior low and closed up 11.57%: a Super Oops: it also closed above the prior day's high. The setup was already there: the stock was above its 200-day, had pulled back 12.6% from its 20-day high, the dip tested the 21 or 50-day average, and the close reclaimed the 21-day average.

The gap day or rally day itself is never the trigger, and the 200-day is not required (owner rulings 2026-10-24/25). Here the drive was an earnings-style gap of 12.9% 7 sessions earlier; the trigger day gapped only 0.95%.

lesson_text: Kicker: the stock is already set up, in an uptrend or a clean base; the day before closes red and WEAK near its low, an almost-failed breakdown with a real body (about 1-5% of price); then the next day gaps up and follows through with a strong green candle that closes above the red day's high and near its own high, usually on a volume surge. The sellers from the red day are trapped. It is short-term positioning and rarely an earnings day: an earnings-day gap is an earnings gapper, a baby red candle before a gap is just a breakout, and a gap against a downtrend is a different setup (owner rulings 2026-10-23/24). Here the stock gapped up 5.92% after a red day and closed up 12.23%, above the prior day's high, at 87% of its range. lesson_text: Oops Reversal (scanner version): opens below the prior close, trades under the prior day's low, then reverses and closes above the prior close. A Williams Oops opens below the prior LOW and rallies back above it. A Super Oops closes above the prior day's HIGH, engulfing the whole day. LOCATION is the main thing: it comes at the end of an orderly drift lower, a flag, a wedge, a double bottom or the end of a downtrend, into a buyable spot, with orderly days before it (no news gap, no outsized red bar) and a technical, not news-sized, Oops day; the Oops-day low must never break afterwards (owner rulings 2026-10-23/24). Here it opened 0.08% from the prior low and closed up 2.71%: a Super Oops: it also closed above the prior day's high. The setup was already there: the stock was above its 200-day, had pulled back 8.0% from its 20-day high, the dip tested the 21 or 50-day average, and the close reclaimed the 21-day average.

Here the stock had corrected 15.3% from its high, the 8, 21 and 50-day averages sat within 1.57% of each other with price 0.6% from the 200-day, the prior 30 closes spanned 10.3%, and the last bar closed up 3.74% above the 20-day high.

lesson_text: Slingshot: a drive first, usually an earnings gapper (it is mostly the way into a power earnings gap after its first pause), sometimes a strong rally; THEN a tight orderly pullback of three to seven sessions, about 5-12% deep, with the closes under the 4-day average of the highs; THEN the trigger, the first close back above that average, a decisive day that closes near its high and needs no gap. The gap day or rally day itself is never the trigger, and the 200-day is not required (owner rulings 2026-10-24/25). Here the drive was an earnings-style gap of 5.9% 18 sessions earlier; the pullback ran 6 sessions and 7.1% deep under the 4-day average of the highs; the trigger day closed up 4.32% at 91% of its range, gapping 2.68%.

lesson_text: High Volume Edge: an up day on a volume that DWARFS everything before it, ten times normal and above the prior record, often on a lesser-known name, the start of a new story; an earnings day counts when the volume is truly massive. That day's close is a LEVEL to mark on the chart, the price the biggest participants committed at; price may trade under it later. It is not an HVC (any high-volume close) and not a PEG (an earnings gap on big but ordinary volume); OPEX and month-end sessions do not count (owner rulings 2026-10-23/25). Here the stock closed up 4.6% on the heaviest volume of the lookback.

lesson_text: Gap Support: a stock that is not in a downtrend gaps up at least 4% on twice its normal volume and holds the gap; days or weeks later it pulls back to the GAP-UP DAY'S LOW and buyers defend it. The best examples hold that low and keep the gap open; a slight breach that closes back above it is still good; a fill down to the gap-fill spot (the prior day's high) that reclaims the low is a lesser example, and a breach that does not reclaim is a failed gap. The gap day itself is a PEG, not gap support, and a gap never revisited is nothing (owner rulings 2026-10-26/27). Here the gap was 12.4% 15 sessions earlier. The test day undercut the gap-up day's low by 7.5% and closed 2.8% under it, 5.1% above the gap top, so the gap stayed open; the close was back above the gap-up low the next session. It was the first test of the gap, and the day closed at 95% of its range.

lesson_text: Gap Support: a stock that is not in a downtrend gaps up at least 4% on twice its normal volume and holds the gap; days or weeks later it pulls back to the GAP-UP DAY'S LOW and buyers defend it. The best examples hold that low and keep the gap open; a slight breach that closes back above it is still good; a fill down to the gap-fill spot (the prior day's high) that reclaims the low is a lesser example, and a breach that does not reclaim is a failed gap. The gap day itself is a PEG, not gap support, and a gap never revisited is nothing (owner rulings 2026-10-26/27). Here the gap was 13.53% 14 sessions earlier. The test day held the gap-up day's low to within 0.5% and closed 10.6% above it, 21.9% above the gap top, so the gap stayed open. It was the first test of the gap, and the day closed at 86% of its range.

lesson_text: Gap Support: a stock that is not in a downtrend gaps up at least 4% on twice its normal volume and holds the gap; days or weeks later it pulls back to the GAP-UP DAY'S LOW and buyers defend it. The best examples hold that low and keep the gap open; a slight breach that closes back above it is still good; a fill down to the gap-fill spot (the prior day's high) that reclaims the low is a lesser example, and a breach that does not reclaim is a failed gap. The gap day itself is a PEG, not gap support, and a gap never revisited is nothing (owner rulings 2026-10-26/27). Here the gap was 11.61% 11 sessions earlier. The test day held the gap-up day's low to within 0.1% and closed 3.8% above it, 11.2% above the gap top, so the gap stayed open. It was the first test of the gap, and the day closed at 76% of its range.

lesson_text: Kicker: the stock is already set up, in an uptrend or a clean base; the day before closes red and WEAK near its low, an almost-failed breakdown with a real body (about 1-5% of price); then the next day gaps up and follows through with a strong green candle that closes above the red day's high and near its own high, usually on a volume surge. The sellers from the red day are trapped. It is short-term positioning and rarely an earnings day: an earnings-day gap is an earnings gapper, a baby red candle before a gap is just a breakout, and a gap against a downtrend is a different setup (owner rulings 2026-10-23/24). Here the stock gapped up 1.71% after a red day and closed up 7.16%, above the prior day's high, at 87% of its range. lesson_text: Oops Reversal (scanner version): opens below the prior close, trades under the prior day's low, then reverses and closes above the prior close. A Williams Oops opens below the prior LOW and rallies back above it. A Super Oops closes above the prior day's HIGH, engulfing the whole day. LOCATION is the main thing: it comes at the end of an orderly drift lower, a flag, a wedge, a double bottom or the end of a downtrend, into a buyable spot, with orderly days before it (no news gap, no outsized red bar) and a technical, not news-sized, Oops day; the Oops-day low must never break afterwards (owner rulings 2026-10-23/24). Here it opened -0.12% from the prior low and closed up 6.25%: a Super Oops: it also closed above the prior day's high. The setup was already there: the stock was above its 200-day, had pulled back 8.3% from its 20-day high, the dip tested the 21 or 50-day average, and the close reclaimed the 21-day average.

lesson_text: Oops Reversal (scanner version): opens below the prior close, trades under the prior day's low, then reverses and closes above the prior close. A Williams Oops opens below the prior LOW and rallies back above it. A Super Oops closes above the prior day's HIGH, engulfing the whole day. LOCATION is the main thing: it comes at the end of an orderly drift lower, a flag, a wedge, a double bottom or the end of a downtrend, into a buyable spot, with orderly days before it (no news gap, no outsized red bar) and a technical, not news-sized, Oops day; the Oops-day low must never break afterwards (owner rulings 2026-10-23/24). Here it opened -0.77% from the prior low and closed up 3.29%: a Super Oops: it also closed above the prior day's high. The setup was already there: the stock was above its 200-day, had pulled back 8.4% from its 20-day high, the dip tested the 21 or 50-day average, and the close reclaimed the 21-day average.

lesson_text: Slingshot: a drive first, usually an earnings gapper (it is mostly the way into a power earnings gap after its first pause), sometimes a strong rally; THEN a tight orderly pullback of three to seven sessions, about 5-12% deep, with the closes under the 4-day average of the highs; THEN the trigger, the first close back above that average, a decisive day that closes near its high and needs no gap. The gap day or rally day itself is never the trigger, and the 200-day is not required (owner rulings 2026-10-24/25). Here the drive was a 30.8% rally that peaked 5 sessions earlier; the pullback ran 4 sessions and 8.9% deep under the 4-day average of the highs; the trigger day closed up 4.47% at 94% of its range, gapping 1.6%.
